transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, the clinical conversational agent. I'm here to help with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. How are you feeling today? Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, I'm doing okay, thank you. I do have some questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start doing light gardening, like watering plants or gentle pruning, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid heavy lifting, bending, or strenuous activities for a month. Also, be careful not to get water in your eyes, especially in the first month after surgery.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thanks for that information. My next question is about my eye gel for dry eyes. When can I start using it again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start using your preservative-free eye drops as prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. It's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, I'll keep that in mind. Another thing I've noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Yes, it's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild, you can try wearing sunglasses when you're outside. However, if it's severe or you have redness and pain in your eye, we may need to assess it further.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for reassuring me. And one last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common to have some blurriness, especially in the first week after surgery. However, if your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay. But generally, your vision should improve quickly and settle down over time.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for all the information. I don't have any more questions for now. You've been very helpful!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure to help. I'm glad I could answer your questions and put your mind at ease. If you do think of anything else or have any concerns, don't hesitate to reach out to your care team. All your questions have been answered. .
